---
title: "BISON benchmarking (parallel)"
output: html_document
---

<!--
  Parallel variant of BISON.Rmd. Same results, but the 24 independent slides
  run concurrently (one worker per slide) instead of serially.

  What changed vs BISON.Rmd, and why:
   * The double for-loop is flattened into a list of independent jobs and run
     with parallel::mclapply (fork-based; Linux only). Each slide is fully
     independent, so this is embarrassingly parallel.
   * calculate_stats() appends to a shared stats.csv (read -> rbind -> write),
     which is NOT safe under parallelism. Instead, each worker returns its
     stats row (via the read-only calculate_ARI/calculate_F1 helpers) and we
     write stats.csv ONCE at the end.
   * plot_annotations() and save_annotations() each write to a unique per-slide
     path, so they remain parallel-safe and are left inside the worker.

  Nothing in models/ is modified. benchmarking_scripts_2.R and constants.R are
  sourced unchanged.
-->


```{r}
suppressMessages({
  library(SingleCellExperiment)
  library(scran)
  library(scater)
  library(Matrix)
  library(purrr)
  library(Rcpp)
  library(RcppArmadillo)
  library(parallel)
  # HDF5Array MUST be loaded in the parent, before mclapply forks. Its .onLoad
  # creates a single global counter file under tempdir(); forked workers share
  # the same tempdir(), so if the first HDF5 access happens *inside* a worker
  # they race to create that one file and all-but-one die with
  # "HDF5Array_dump_names_global_counter ... already exists". Loading it here
  # runs .onLoad once in the parent; children inherit the counter file.
  library(HDF5Array)
})

## Load BISON
old_wd <- getwd()
setwd("models/BISON")
source("R/utils.R")
source("R/main.R")
setwd(old_wd)

## Loader helper functions
source("benchmarking_scripts_2.R")
source("constants.R")
```

```{r}
model <- "BISON"

datasets <- list(
  "DLPFC" = DLPFC_files,
  # "HER2+" = HER2_files,
  "MOSTA" = MOSTA_files
  # "Mouse hypothalamus" = mouse_hypothalamus_files
)

loaders <- list(
  "DLPFC" = load_DLPFC,
  "HER2+" = load_HER2,
  "MOSTA" = load_MOSTA
)

platforms <- list(
  DLPFC     = "Visium",
  `HER2+`   = "ST",
  MOSTA     = "ST"
)
```

```{r}
## Flatten the (dataset, slide) grid into a list of independent jobs.
jobs <- list()
for (dataset_name in names(datasets)) {
  for (file in names(datasets[[dataset_name]])) {
    jobs[[length(jobs) + 1]] <- list(dataset_name = dataset_name, file = file)
  }
}

## One worker per slide. There are only ~24 slides, so cap at the job count.
n_cores <- min(length(jobs), max(1, detectCores() - 1))

## Runs one slide end-to-end and RETURNS its stats row (no shared writes here).
run_one <- function(job) {
  dataset_name <- job$dataset_name
  file         <- job$file

  loader   <- loaders[[dataset_name]]
  platform <- platforms[[dataset_name]]

  result <- tryCatch({
    loaded     <- loader(file)
    sce        <- loaded$sce
    n_clusters <- loaded$n_clusters

    sce <- preprocess_data(sce, file)

    out <- run_BISON(
      sce,
      level       = n_clusters,
      platform    = platform,
      n_top_genes = 1000,
      K           = n_clusters,
      R_          = n_clusters,   # gene-cluster count; see run_BISON()'s docstring
      n_iters     = 100,
      seed        = 1,
      export_path = sprintf(
        "annotation_results/%s/%s_%s_annotations.csv",
        model, dataset_name, file
      )
    )

    # Unique per-slide output path -> parallel-safe, keep inside the worker.
    plot_annotations(
      out$sce,
      model = model, level = n_clusters, predicted = out$predicted_key,
      tissue = dataset_name, slide = file,
      export_path = file.path("figures", "spatial", model,
                              sprintf("%s_%s_predicted_plot.png", dataset_name, file))
    )

    # Read-only stat helpers -> compute here, but DON'T write the shared csv.
    ari <- calculate_ARI(out$sce, out$predicted_key)
    f1  <- calculate_F1(out$sce, out$predicted_key)

    data.frame(
      Model = model, Dataset = dataset_name, Slide = file,
      ARI = ari, F1_Weighted = f1$f1_weighted, F1_Score = f1$f1_macro
    )
  }, error = function(e) {
    # Don't let one bad slide kill the whole run; surface it in the results.
    data.frame(
      Model = model, Dataset = dataset_name, Slide = file,
      ARI = NA_real_, F1_Weighted = NA_real_, F1_Score = NA_real_,
      error = conditionMessage(e)
    )
  })

  result
}

rows <- mclapply(jobs, run_one, mc.cores = n_cores, mc.preschedule = FALSE)
```

```{r}
## Defensive: if any worker returned a non-data.frame (e.g. a hard fork crash,
## which surfaces as a try-error), coerce it into an error row so it can't sink
## the whole run's output at bind_rows.
rows <- Map(function(r, job) {
  if (is.data.frame(r)) return(r)
  data.frame(
    Model = model, Dataset = job$dataset_name, Slide = job$file,
    ARI = NA_real_, F1_Weighted = NA_real_, F1_Score = NA_real_,
    error = paste("worker returned non-data.frame:",
                  paste(utils::head(as.character(r), 3), collapse = " | "))
  )
}, rows, jobs)

new_stats <- dplyr::bind_rows(rows)  # tolerates the optional `error` column

## Merge into stats.csv WITHOUT clobbering other models' rows: drop any existing
## BISON rows (so re-runs replace rather than duplicate), keep everything else
## (e.g. SpaRTaCo), then append this run. Written exactly once.
if (file.exists("stats.csv")) {
  existing <- read.csv("stats.csv", check.names = FALSE)
  existing <- existing[existing$Model != model, , drop = FALSE]
  stats <- dplyr::bind_rows(existing, new_stats)
} else {
  stats <- new_stats
}

print(new_stats)
write.csv(stats, "stats.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
